title: Increment and Decrement Expressions
summary: Shows the programming-only shorthand operators ++, --, +=, -=, *= and /= as compact forms of reassigning a variable.

concepts.heading: Increment and decrement
points: x++ is shorthand for x = x + 1 (increment). With x at 5 it becomes 6.
x-- is shorthand for x = x - 1 (decrement). With x at 5 it becomes 4.
These only ever change the value by exactly one.
(Extra) The name of C++ is a nod to this operator: C plus one.

concepts.heading: Compound assignment operators
points: x += 2 is the same as x = x + 2; use it to change by more than one.
The right side can be another variable: x += y means x = x + y.
The same pattern exists for -=, *= and /=, each applying its operator and storing the result back in the left variable.

code_examples.caption: Reference repo demo (prefix form and compound assignments)
code_examples.code:
var a = 5, b = 5, c = 5, d = 5, e = 5;
console.log(a + 1); // 6, a unchanged
console.log(++b);   // 6
console.log(--c);   // 4
console.log(d += 2);// 7
console.log(e -= 2);// 3

pitfalls: (Extra) a + 1 on its own does not change a; only ++, -- and the assignment operators do.
(Extra) x++ (postfix) returns the old value while ++x (prefix) returns the new one; matters only when the expression's value is used, as in console.log.
